goal.title: Scan goal
goal.text: Is the sample project ready to move from PHP 7.1 to PHP 8.5.12, and what has to change first?
points: Code that no longer runs or behaves differently on 8.5.12
Libraries and extensions that block the upgrade
Proof on PHP 8.5.12 itself (php -l and class loading)

scope.v: Running the application or its tests

summary: Not ready yet. One compile error was fixed between the two scans, which revealed the next one: php -l stops at the first parse error per file. The remaining blockers are two compile errors, three removed PHP features, the mcrypt extension and four outdated libraries. composer-app compiles cleanly but one class fails to load on 8.5.12.
steps: Fix the three compile errors so the file loads at all (one done in the second scan).
Replace the PHP 4 constructor, each() and mysql_* (see the notes, with tested code).
Replace mcrypt with openssl or sodium; verify old data still decrypts.
Upgrade or replace the libraries marked Not supported / Upgrade.
Run Rector for the deprecations (implicit nullable, (integer)), then re-scan: a new version is added and the report shows what was resolved.
For values from the database, read the error log of a run on PHP 8.5.12 (audit.php --logs): logs-app shows a fatal error and NULL arguments that only the logs reveal.
Run the test suite on PHP 8.5.12 with error_reporting(E_ALL) before switching production.

notes.title: About this sample
notes.body: Generated by examples/build.sh from fixtures/legacy-app (deliberately broken PHP 7 code, two scans: the second ran on a copy with the curly brace offset fixed, to show the version selector and the resolved / new counts) and fixtures/composer-app (runtime proof: every class loaded on PHP 8.5.12).
